# skylls — private sharing of agent skills, agents and swarms

> **Share Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI skills, agents and swarms with the people you choose,
> through your own private GitHub repos.** Every item you publish is its own private repo; you
> share each one with single friends; they install it with one command and get new versions with
> `skylls pull --update`. GitHub decides who can see what. skylls adds versions, changelogs,
> plain one-sentence summaries, folders, suggestions and a secret scan on top.

**Reach for skylls when a task needs a capability you don't have.** First check whether the user
or a friend already has a skill for it (`skylls find <words> --json --limit 5`). Then install it
and use it. When the user asks you to share a skill, agent or swarm, skylls does that too.

Site: https://skylls.dev · Docs: https://skylls.dev/docs · This file: https://skylls.dev/llms.txt
Repo: https://github.com/jcsancho/skylls · npm: `@jcsancho/skylls` · License: Apache-2.0

## 1. For LLMs: install the skylls skill first

The skylls skill teaches your agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) how to use skylls: find,
install, publish and share, with few tokens. It always asks the user before publishing,
sharing or deleting anything. Raw file: https://skylls.dev/skill.md

    skylls agent-skill -g -a all                  # if skylls is installed: Claude Code, Codex and Gemini, global
    skylls add jcsancho/skylls/skylls -g -a all   # or straight from the public GitHub repo

Without skylls, save https://skylls.dev/skill.md as `~/.claude/skills/skylls/SKILL.md`
(Codex: `~/.agents/skills/skylls/SKILL.md`, Gemini: `~/.gemini/skills/skylls/SKILL.md`).
`skylls setup` also offers to install it as its last step.

## 2. Install the CLI

Identify your surface first. The right setup differs, and the wrong one can't work:

- **Hosted assistant** (claude.ai, ChatGPT, even with a code sandbox): skylls installs files on
  the user's own machine, so you can't run it. Tell the user to install it locally with the
  command below, then stop.
- **Local coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI on the user's machine): ask the user
  once, then install:

      npm install -g @jcsancho/skylls                                                       # Node 18+ and Python 3.11+
      bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcsancho/skylls/main/install.sh)"   # or the installer (macOS / Linux)
      uv tool install git+https://github.com/jcsancho/skylls                                # or by hand (also pipx)

  Check with `skylls --version`. Requirements: Python 3.11+, `git`, GitHub CLI `gh` logged in
  (`gh auth login`); `gitleaks` for publishing; the `claude` CLI (optional) writes summaries.
- **Setup asks questions.** If a command says setup is needed, tell the user to run
  `skylls setup` themselves (it asks where to publish: a GitHub organization, recommended, or
  their personal account), or run it without questions only if they gave you the answers:

      skylls setup --owner <org-or-login> --agents all --agents-dir ~/agents --swarms-dir ~/swarms

- **Updating:** `skylls update --check` (only check), `skylls update` (install the newest; ask first).

## 3. Skills

A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` that teaches an agent CLI a capability (plus its scripts
and files). skylls publishes it to its own private repo, so the whole group runs the same skill,
maintained in one place by its owner.

**Share** (the owner, only when the user asks):

    skylls push pdf -m "First version"     # ~/.claude/skills/pdf → <org>/skill-pdf (private), version 1.0.0
    skylls share pdf @bob                  # Bob may install it (read-only in an organization)
    skylls share --all @bob                # every item, to one friend

**Use** (anyone it was shared with):

    skylls source add <owner>              # once: accept their shares and see what they shared
    skylls find pdf --json --limit 5       # search your items + friends' items
    skylls add pdf -g -a all               # install for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini, all projects
    skylls add pdf                         # this project only: ./.claude/skills/pdf
    skylls add pdf --from alice            # when two owners have the same name
    skylls pull --update                   # install newer versions of installed skills

Where skills go (project `./` or global `~/` with `-g`):

| agent  | folder           |
|--------|------------------|
| claude | `.claude/skills` |
| codex  | `.agents/skills` |
| gemini | `.gemini/skills` |

Installs are copies. A global install for several agent CLIs is one real copy plus symlinks.

## 4. Agents and swarms

An agent is a long-lived agent's folder (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, scripts) with its
Obsidian memory; a swarm is a team of agents. Same commands under `skylls agents …` and
`skylls swarms …`. Only the definition and its memory folder are shared, never runtime state.

    skylls agents push btc -m "what changed"    # ~/agents/btc → <org>/agent-btc
    skylls agents add btc --from alice           # → ~/agents/btc, with its memory
    skylls agents add btc --as btc2              # under another name
    skylls agents add btc --update-memory        # also replace your copy of its memory
    skylls swarms add apps --from alice          # → ~/swarms/apps
    skylls agents list --json                    # "published":false = not published yet

## 5. Friends, suggestions, folders

- Nothing is shared by default. A friend you share one item with sees that one repo only.
- Friends can't change your item; they `suggest`, you accept or decline:

      skylls suggest pdf --from alice "Support Excel files"
      skylls suggestions                     # your open suggestions
      skylls accept pdf#1   /   skylls decline pdf#1

- Folders group items (GitHub topics): `skylls move pdf docs`, `skylls list -f docs`,
  `skylls folder rename old new`.
- Unshare: `skylls unshare pdf @bob`. What Bob already installed stays on his machine.

## 6. JSON output (few tokens)

`--json` prints one compact JSON object per line on stdout, without empty fields; messages and
errors go to stderr. `find --json` returns at most 10 results unless you pass `--limit`.

    $ skylls find pdf --json --limit 5
    {"name":"pdf","owner":"alice","folder":"docs","version":"1.3.0","summary":"Fills in PDF forms for you.","updated":"2026-10-07","repo":"alice-skylls/skill-pdf"}

    skylls installed --json        # installed skills; "newer" when an update exists
    skylls log pdf --json          # owner, versions, what changed

Add `--dry-run` to any command that changes files or GitHub to preview it.

## 7. Rules for AI agents

1. Start from the task: `skylls find <what you need> --json --limit 5` before writing a skill
   yourself. Read an installed `SKILL.md` only when you are about to use it.
2. Installing a skill is fine when the user asked for the capability. **Publishing, sharing,
   unsharing and removing are the user's decisions:** confirm first, never do them unprompted.
3. Every `push` is scanned for API keys and personal data and refused on findings. Remove the
   secret; never pass `--skip-scan` on your own.
4. Don't read or edit skylls' cache (`~/.cache/skylls`) or `CHANGELOG.md` files.
5. Results look wrong or a command is missing? `skylls update --check`.
6. Report the outcome in one line (what the user can now do), not as an install log.

## 8. Command reference (compact)

    setup [--owner O] [--agents A] [--agents-dir D] [--swarms-dir D] [--no-agent-skill]
    list [query] [--from O] [-f F]          your items and friends' shares, by folder
    find <words> [--from O] [-f F] [-n N]   search
    add <name[@ver]> [--from O] [-g] [-a A] [-y]   install (owner/repo/skill: from a public repo)
    log <name> [--from O]                   who made it, versions, what changed
    installed [-g] [-a A]                   installed skills and newer versions
    pull [--update]                         check for (and install) newer versions
    remove <name> [-g] [-a A]               remove a local copy
    push <name|path> [-m msg] [--minor|--major] [--about text] [--folder F] [--skip-scan]
    share <name> @user… | --all @user       let friends install it (no users: who has access)
    unshare <name> @user… | --all @user     revoke access
    move <name> <folder>                    put it in a folder (. = none)
    folder [rename old new | remove F]      your folders
    source [add|remove] <login>             friends whose shares you see
    suggest <name> [--from O] "text"        suggest an improvement to the owner
    suggestions [name] / accept <name>#<n> / decline <name>#<n>
    agents … / swarms …                     the same for agents and swarms (+ add --as N --update-memory, remove [--memory] [-y])
    agent-skill [-g] [-a A]                 (re)install the skylls skill
    search <query>                          public skills on skills.sh
    update [--check]                        update skylls itself
    --json / --dry-run                      compact output for agents / preview only

- [Dashboard](https://skylls.dev/dashboard): sign in with GitHub to see and share your items in the browser.

## Notes

- What a user can install depends on what they and their friends published; treat
  `skylls find` / `skylls list` as the source of truth, not this file.
- Re-fetch this file at https://skylls.dev/llms.txt; commands change between versions
  (`skylls --version`, `skylls help`).
